messages:
frank: Morning — saw a wave of immediate preemptions in ap-southeast1 during the autoscaler churn. Lots of tiny 1-GPU jobs get evicted right after binding, then reschedule and get evicted again. Suspect handoff timing between provisioner and scheduler.

maya: Ah — saw similar spikes on the dashboard. Can you drop the grafana link?

frank: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/cluster/evictions?orgId=1&var-region=ap-southeast1 — notice binding->evict latency is <2s for a bunch of pods.

sam: digging through scheduler logs: scheduler issues a preemptive eviction almost immediately when a higher-priority pod arrives on the same node. There's no grace/handoff window currently. Warm-node removal was also happening in parallel.

leila: Suggestion: introduce a short "handoff window" (e.g. 20-45s) where recently-bound pods are soft-protected from preemption to let node warm-up and sidecars finish. That should cut dup executions for short jobs.

maya: +1. We need metrics first. Add binding_start -> eviction_time histogram and a counter for "evict_after_bind".

frank: I'll prototype a scheduler flag: handoff_window_seconds and soft_protect=true. If the higher-priority pod still needs the node after the window, normal preemption proceeds. Keeps behavior predictable.

leila: config sketch: 
```
scheduler:
  preemption:
    handoff_window_seconds: 30
    soft_protect: true
```

sam: Important: gate behind feature flag and canary to a couple of regions. We should avoid global rollout until we see effects on binpacking efficiency.

maya: I'll add telemetry: scheduler.binding_evict_latency_seconds histogram, label by region+node_pool, and a derived alert if evict_after_bind_rate > 0.5% over 10m.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary scheduled — scheduler/handoff-window feature-flag will be enabled in ap-southeast1 and eu-west1 at 2025-11-03T03:00Z for 10% of clusters.

sam: Cost note: current churn appears to add ~3–5% extra GPU-hours in ap-southeast1 last week (rough estimate). Reducing immediate evicts should save both cost and scheduler churn.

sre-oncall: Oncall: create a short-playbook for rollback if pack/unpack increases node pressure or latency regressions appear. Alert: increase in pending pods >5% after rollout.

frank: I'll draft rollout doc + perf harness to simulate tiny-gang workloads and measure packing/regret. @maya please add the metrics, @sam can you review the placement heuristics changes.

leila: I'll open the PR with unit tests and the feature flag. Will include telemetry hooks and a small local simulator to test edge cases.

maya: Thx — once metrics land I'll run a quick analysis on last 7 days to pick the best default for handoff_window_seconds. Propose starting at 30s.

sam: Ack. If canary looks good, roll to 50% then full. Watch binpacking efficiency dashboards.

frank: Great. I'll post the rollout plan + links here when draft is ready.

leila: :thumbsup:

ops-bot: incident-bot: Note — no active incident. Monitoring changes planned.

frank: FYI, the immediate next step: telemetry + PR. Tracking in #eng-platform-runbooks.
